figures.caption: Figure 1: Projections of representative singular orbits Γ(0,0) (dark green trajectories) onto (n, q, V )-space, with (A-C) q = 0.490917 < qCDH and (D) q = qCDH. The lower panel of (A) plots the function ḡ2(q) over the 0 ≤ q < qCDH, showing (3.7) has no equilibrium. Panels (B)-(D) show the perturbed bursting solutions Γ(ε,δ) (black trajectories) with different perturbation sizes: the upper panels show their projections onto (n, q, V )-space, and the lower panels show the voltage traces in time. The parameter values are (B) (ε, δ) = (0.03, 6×10−7) with (rε, rδ) = (10, 10−5), (C) (ε, δ) = (0.03, 6 × 10−4) with (rε, rδ) = (10, 0.01), and (D) (ε, δ) = (0.031, 0.06) with (rε, rδ) = (10.397, 1). Also shown are the critical manifold Ms (blue surface) and the superslow manifold Mss (red curve). Ms is divided into three sheets by the fold curves Ls (blue curves): the attracting lower sheet ML s and the repelling middle and upper sheets (MM s and MU s ). Mss consists of an attracting branch Ma ss (solid) and a repelling branch M r ss (dashed). The lower fold Ls intersects Mss at the CDH singularity (yellow square). The cyan surfaces represent the periodic attractor Ps, which emanates from a curve of supercritical Hopf bifurcation on MU s (not shown) and terminates at the homoclinic bifurcation (HC, light green curve). The DHB and the folded node (FN) are denoted by the red diamond and blue circle, respectively. In panel (D), the trajectory enters the funnel (shaded region) of the folded node, which is bounded by the lower fold curve Ls and the singular strong canard (magenta curve). Note that the displayed q range varies across panels.

Figure 2: Effects of variations in the fast timescales rε on the dynamics of (2.4). (A) Oneparameter bifurcation diagram of the full system (2.4) with respect to rε for rδ = 1. Other parameters are fixed at their default values in Table 1. The solid (resp., dashed) black curve denotes stable (resp., unstable) full-system equilibria. The red diamond denotes the fullsystem Hopf bifurcation (HB), giving rise to a periodic orbit branch (cyan). This branch changes stability from stable (solid) to unstable (dashed) at a torus bifurcation (TR, purple circle). Isolas of MMO- and MMBO-type periodic oscillations are shown above the cyan branch (solid: stable, dashed: unstable). The inset shows the enlarged views of the gray, brown, orange, and light blue isolas. (B) Enlarged view of the isolas corresponding to MMBO orbits with 6-SAOs (orange), 5-SAOs (light blue), 4-SAOs (green), and 3-SAOs (pink). Along each isola, stable segments (solid curves) lie between a period-doubling bifurcation (PD, red star) and a saddle-node bifurcation of periodic orbits (SNPO, blue circle). (C)-(D) Example voltage traces of (2.4) for different values of rε.

Figure 3: Effects of variations in the fast and superslow timescales, rε and rδ, on the dynamics of (2.4). (A) As rε and rδ are varied over the ranges 0.1 ≤ rε ≤ 10 and 0.1 ≤ rδ ≤ 10, the full system exhibits different activity patterns: quiescence (dark blue region), SAOs without spiking (light blue region), MMOs (cyan region), MMBOs (yellow region), bursting (orange region), and mixed MMO-MMBO type (red region). Also shown are the full-system Hopf bifurcation curve (red curve) and four SNPO curves corresponding to 1s MMOs with s ≥ 1 (dashed dark green, pink, purple, and blue curves). The magenta star marks MMOs obtained at the default timescales (Fig. 2D, top panel). (B) Enlarged view of the two-parameter bifurcation curves of the SNPO (dashed green, same curve as in panel (A)) and PD (solid red) associated with the stable 14 orbit segment. Partial isolas for fixed rδ = 1 and rδ = 6 are shown in the insets.

Figure 4: Different projections of an attracting MMO solution of the full-system (2.4) for (rε, rδ) = (1, 1), with default (εi, δ) values given in Table 3. (A) In (n, q, V )-space, the critical manifold Ms (blue surface), two fold curves Ls (blue curves), the superslow manifold Mss (red curve), the periodic attractor Ps (cyan surface), and the homoclinic bifurcation curve (light green curve) have the same meaning as in Fig. 1. The superslow manifold Mss changes stability from attracting (red solid) to repelling (red dashed) at the HB (red diamond). Along the lower fold curve, a folded node (FN, blue circle) is located O(δ) close to the CDH (yellow square). The magenta circle is a full-system equilibrium (TE), which is a saddle-focus. (B) Two-dimensional (2D) cross-sections of the Ms and Ps in the (n, V )- space, with q fixed at its minimum (cyan curves) and maximum (orange curves) values. (C) Projection of the curves of the fold Ls, Mss, and the HC, together with FN, CDH, and HB, TE points, and the trajectory onto the (n, q)-space.

Figure 5: Time traces of (2.4) illustrating MMO-MMBO transitions as the three-timescale separation increases. (A) For fixed rδ = 1, increasing rε from rε = 1 (top) to rε = 1.65 (middle) and rε = 5 (bottom). (B) For fixed rε = 1, decreasing rδ from rδ = 1 (top) to rδ = 0.6 (middle) and rδ = 0.2 (bottom). Other parameters are given in Tables 1 and 2.

Figure 6: Projections of the periodic MMBO solutions of (2.4) from Fig. 5A onto (n, q, V )- space (left panels) and (n, q)-plane (right panels), together with the corresponding geometric structures, for rδ = 1 and (A, B) rε = 1.65 and (C, D) rε = 5. Increasing rε shifts the SAO mechanism from the DHB (A, B) to the CDH (C, D) by bringing the DHB (red diamond) closer to the CDH (yellow square), allowing the trajectory to enter the funnel (shaded region) of the FN (blue circle) before passing through the CDH and the DHB. Other colors and symbols have the same meaning as in Figs. 1 and 4.

Figure 7: Projections of the attracting MMBO solutions of (2.4) from Fig. 5B onto (n, q, V )- space (left panels) and (n, q)-plane (right panels), together with the corresponding geometric structures, for rε = 1 and (A, B) rδ = 0.6 and (C, D) rδ = 0.2. Decreasing rδ leads to increasingly pronounced DHB-like features. Although the FN (blue circle) moves closer to the CDH (yellow square), the trajectory remains outside the funnel of the FN and the neighborhood of the CDH. Other colors and symbols have the same meaning as in Figs. 1 and 4.

Figure 8: Time traces of (2.4) illustrating the persistence of MMOs as the three-timescale separation is weakened. (A) For fixed rδ = 1, decreasing rε from rε = 1 (top) to rε = 0.65 (bottom). (B) For fixed rε = 0.65, increasing rδ from rδ = 3 (top) to rδ = 10 (bottom).

Figure 9: Projections of the attracting MMO solutions of (2.4) from Fig. 8 onto (A) (n, q, V )- space and (B) (n, q, Cai)-space, together with the corresponding geometric structures, for fixed rε = 0.65 and different values of rδ. The black curve represents the projection of the trajectory from Fig. 8A (bottom) with rδ = 1. The brown and cyan curves indicate the projections of the trajectories from Fig. 8B with rδ = 3 and rδ = 10, respectively. Other colors and symbols have the same meaning as in Figs. 1 and 4.

Figure 10: Time traces of solutions of 2.4 (left panels) and their projections onto (n, q)plane together with the corresponding geometric structures (right panels) for rε = 7.5, (A) rδ = 0.9, (B) rδ = 3, and (C) rδ = 6. Increasing rδ produces SAOs with more pronounced canard-like features while gradually weakening DHB characteristics. When rδ is sufficiently large (e.g., rδ = 6), the folded node FN transitions to a folded focus FF, leading to the loss of SAOs. Other colors and symbols have the same meaning as in Fig. 4C.

Figure 11: The CDH represents the interaction between the canard and DHB mechanisms. (A) The folded singularities (blue curve) of (C.25) converge to the CDH (yellow curve) as rδ → 0 (equivalently, δ → 0). The blue curve consists of folded nodes (solid) and folded foci (dashed), separated by a degenerate folded node (DFN). (B) The DHB (red curve) of (C.28) converges to the CDH (yellow curve) as rε → ∞ (equivalently, ε → 0).
